sub_graphs.name: Transaction Gas Limit Constant
sub_graphs.description: Defines the protocol-level constant MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT = 16,777,216 (2^24) that caps the maximum gas any single transaction may specify.

invariants.text: MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT = 2^24 = 16,777,216 gas. This value is a fixed protocol constant independent of the block gas limit.
The transaction gas cap is strictly less than the block gas limit, ensuring multiple transactions can fit within each block.

state_variables.name: MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT
state_variables.description: Protocol-level constant: maximum gas limit per transaction (2^24).

sub_graphs.name: Transaction Pool Validation
sub_graphs.description: During transaction validation at the txpool level, any transaction with gasLimit exceeding 16,777,216 is invalidated and not included in the txpool.

invariants.text: No transaction in the txpool may have a gasLimit > MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT (16,777,216).

functions.description: Validates that tx.gasLimit <= MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT. Returns false (rejects) if gasLimit exceeds the cap. Rejected transactions return error code MAX_GAS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

pre_conditions.text: A transaction is submitted to the txpool with a specified gasLimit field.

post_conditions.text: If tx.gasLimit > 16,777,216, the transaction is rejected with MAX_GAS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and NOT added to the txpool.
If tx.gasLimit <= 16,777,216, the transaction proceeds through normal validation (other checks still apply).

state_transitions.description: Transaction is invalidated and not included in the txpool.
Transaction passes gas limit check and continues to further validation.

sub_graphs.name: Block Validation
sub_graphs.description: During block validation before processing, any block containing a transaction with gasLimit > 16,777,216 is deemed invalid and rejected.

invariants.text: A valid block must not contain any transaction with gasLimit > MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT (16,777,216).

functions.description: Iterates over all transactions in the block and verifies each has gasLimit <= 16,777,216. If any transaction exceeds the cap, the entire block is deemed invalid and rejected.

pre_conditions.text: A block is received containing one or more transactions, each with a gasLimit field.

post_conditions.text: If any transaction in the block has gasLimit > 16,777,216, the entire block is rejected as invalid.
If all transactions in the block have gasLimit <= 16,777,216, the block passes this validation step.

state_transitions.condition: exists tx in block where tx.gasLimit > 16,777,216
state_transitions.description: Block is deemed invalid and rejected before processing.
Block passes gas limit validation and proceeds to further block processing.

sub_graphs.name: Security: DoS Mitigation via Gas Cap
sub_graphs.description: The gas cap mitigates DoS attack vectors by preventing a single transaction from consuming most or all of the block gas, ensuring fairer gas allocation and more predictable block validation times.

invariants.text: No single transaction can consume more than approximately half of a typical block's gas (30-40M gas), since the cap is 16,777,216.
Block verification times are bounded more predictably because no single transaction can dominate execution.

sub_graphs.name: ModExp Multiplication Complexity Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Calculates the multiplication complexity factor based on base_length and modulus_length. Introduces a minimum complexity of 16 and doubles the complexity when max(base_length, modulus_length) > 32 bytes.

functions.description: Computes multiplication complexity. max_length = max(base_length, modulus_length); words = ceil(max_length / 8); if max_length > 32: return 2 * words^2; else return 16.
functions.code:
def calculate_multiplication_complexity(base_length, modulus_length):
    max_length = max(base_length, modulus_length)
    words = math.ceil(max_length / 8)
    multiplication_complexity = 16
    if max_length > 32: multiplication_complexity = 2 * words**2
    return multiplication_complexity

pre_conditions.text: base_length and modulus_length are non-negative integers derived from the ModExp precompile input.

sub_graphs.name: ModExp Iteration Count Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Calculates the iteration count based on exponent_length and the exponent value. Doubles the multiplier for exponents > 32 bytes from 8 to 16.

invariants.text: iteration_count >= 1 for all valid inputs (ensured by max(iteration_count, 1)).
When exponent_length <= 32 and exponent == 0, iteration_count = 1 (due to max(..., 1)).

functions.description: Computes iteration count. If exponent_length <= 32 and exponent == 0: 0. If exponent_length <= 32: exponent.bit_length() - 1. If exponent_length > 32: (16 * (exponent_length - 32)) + ((exponent & (2^256 - 1)).bit_length() - 1). Result is max'd with 1.

pre_conditions.text: exponent_length is a non-negative integer. exponent is the actual exponent value from the ModExp precompile input.

sub_graphs.name: ModExp Gas Cost Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Computes the final gas cost for the ModExp precompile (address 0x05) by combining multiplication_complexity and iteration_count. Minimum gas is 500 (increased from 200). Division by 3 is removed, tripling the general cost.

invariants.text: gas_cost >= 500 for all ModExp precompile calls (minimum gas floor).
gas_cost = max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)). No division by 3 is applied.

functions.description: Final gas cost: max(500, floor(calculate_multiplication_complexity(base_length, modulus_length) * calculate_iteration_count(exponent_length, exponent))).

state_variables.name: MODEXP_PRECOMPILE_ADDRESS
state_variables.description: The address of the ModExp precompile contract.

state_variables.name: MIN_GAS_COST
state_variables.description: Minimum gas cost for any ModExp call (increased from 200 in EIP-2565).

pre_conditions.text: A call is made to the ModExp precompile at address 0x05 with base_length, modulus_length, exponent_length, and exponent as inputs.

post_conditions.text: The caller is charged gas_cost = max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)).

sub_graphs.name: Delta from EIP-2565 Pricing
sub_graphs.description: Summarizes the three specific changes from the EIP-2565 pricing algorithm: (1) minimum gas 200->500 and removal of /3, (2) large exponent multiplier 8->16, (3) minimum complexity of 16 with 2x multiplier for >32 byte inputs.

invariants.text: Change 1: Minimum gas increased from 200 to 500 (150% increase). Division by 3 removed, tripling general cost (200% increase).
Change 2: For exponents > 32 bytes, the multiplier in iteration_count changed from 8 to 16 (doubled).
Change 3: Minimum multiplication_complexity is now 16 (was words^2 which could be as low as 1). For max_length > 32, complexity is 2*words^2 (was words^2).
